claims.claim: Seventeen eligible studies provide the direct evidence synthesis
claims.assessment: The exact search, exclusions and extraction matrix are missing locally; the 17-study completeness claim is not independently verified.

claims.claim: Mathematical programming offers feasibility and bounds for the stated model
claims.assessment: Solver bounds apply to the formulated model and tolerances; they do not validate omitted physics or real operation.

claims.claim: Shared hubs and modes can improve infrastructure sharing under conditions
claims.assessment: The mechanism is conditional on utilization, phasing, participation and access. No universal saving or local service allocation follows.

claims.claim: No universal ranking of AI, metaheuristics and conventional methods is established
claims.assessment: The authors explicitly avoid ranking incomparable studies. The missing eligible matrix and originals still qualify the evidence census.

claims.claim: Climate observations and Paris temperature goals motivate mitigation
claims.assessment: The cited observations and treaty are unverified here. Temperature goals are policy context rather than model results.

claims.claim: IEA capture and storage capacity growth between the 2025 and 2026 updates
claims.assessment: The claim concerns operational plus under-construction capacity. Its project-database attribution needs reconciliation with the ETP reference.

claims.claim: Operational facilities reportedly grew 54%, with 27 new facilities in 2025
claims.assessment: The snapshot is unverified. Under a common population, 27 divided by 54% implies 50 previous facilities; this is only conditional arithmetic.

claims.claim: CCUS is discussed as a pathway for hard-to-abate process sectors
claims.assessment: This is attributed pathway context, not proof of net benefit for every technology, sector or site.

claims.claim: Transport and storage are described as major cost components
claims.assessment: Cost shares depend on the case boundary. The inspected Budiarto original reports capture as roughly 80% of full-chain cost.

claims.claim: Spatial mismatch and topology create interdependent planning decisions
claims.assessment: The original SimCCS supports the coupling mechanism. This does not validate a Japanese network or physical storage service.

claims.claim: Most studies reportedly isolate matching or networks and remain static
claims.assessment: Main text does not quantify these literature frequencies. Verification needs the eligible-study matrix and original formulations.

claims.claim: No framework is said to integrate the entire planning and operating process
claims.assessment: This broad absence claim requires a defined decision horizon and eligible corpus, rather than titles or contextual citations alone.

claims.claim: Table 1 compares this review with five earlier reviews
claims.assessment: The five earlier reviews were not inspected here. Partial coverage is a scope label, not a quality score.

claims.claim: The search applies no database filters and uses DOI/title-year deduplication
claims.assessment: The stated protocol is readable, but exact strings, exports, normalization and database versions are unavailable locally.

claims.claim: The reported screening and exclusion counts reconcile
claims.assessment: All reported arithmetic identities reconcile. Search retrieval, deduplication and individual screening decisions are not reproduced.

claims.claim: Eligibility permits partial coupled decisions and requires geological storage
claims.assessment: This is the explicit operational definition. Contextual CCU or AI examples are not automatically direct eligible evidence.

claims.claim: The 17 reports are described as all eligible reports, rather than chosen examples
claims.assessment: The report-level log and full matrix are needed. Table 6 has five examples and is not the complete included set.

claims.claim: The protocol declines pooled effects, inferred missing values and unsupported rankings
claims.assessment: These are explicit protocol safeguards. They do not independently verify the underlying extraction or assessment.

claims.claim: General source–sink matching is described as NP-hard
claims.assessment: Hard mixed-integer formulations do not imply every transport subcase is hard. A precise reduction and complexity assumptions are needed.

claims.claim: Source and storage geography constrains network choices
claims.assessment: Resource mass, annual rate, physical safety and commercial access remain distinct. The cited geographic sources are unverified.

claims.claim: Irreversible early choices can create lock-in and underutilization
claims.assessment: The risk is case dependent; no calibrated outage probability or universal benefit is supplied.

claims.claim: Hubs can reduce duplicated assets and improve utilization
claims.assessment: Fixed-charge sharing can help, but participation, minimum utilization and cost recovery can change the result.

claims.claim: Cement–methanol production illustrates hydrogen and CCUS coupling
claims.assessment: The native energy and product case is unverified. Product fate, hydrogen alternatives and operating profiles matter.

claims.claim: Earlier continuous-time models address timing, injection rates and resource capacity
claims.assessment: Tan 2013 is not inspected here. The methodological claim does not supply an annual physical dataset.

claims.claim: Cost, safety, reliability and redundancy can create competing objectives
claims.assessment: This is a modelling requirement, not a measured safety or reliability bound.

claims.claim: Time-indexed optimization, scenarios, monitoring and decision support differ
claims.assessment: The distinction is useful. A time index does not alone establish feedback control, recourse or endogenous participation.

claims.claim: GeoCapacity, NETL and Chinese databases support larger-scale studies
claims.assessment: Coverage, versions and actual database contents remain unverified. Resource atlases are not injection histories.

claims.claim: Early SimCCS jointly selects capture, pipelines and storage
claims.assessment: The scoped original supports joint decisions on a lifetime basis; it explicitly has no temporal component.

claims.claim: Later models add periods, supply-chain scope and uncertainty
claims.assessment: These are method summaries. Each original's decision domains, uncertainties and physical constraints still need verification.

claims.claim: Clustering and decomposition can reduce model size
claims.assessment: Aggregation may reduce model size, but it can introduce approximation and feasibility losses. Hierarchy alone is not an optimality certificate.

claims.claim: DRL is proposed for repeated operational decisions through an MDP
claims.assessment: The text calls this prospective. No trained CCUS network policy or controlled performance advantage is supplied.

claims.claim: PINNs can support component simulation and state estimation
claims.assessment: Physics penalties do not certify discrete-network, legal or emergency constraints. Actual trained cases and benchmark domains remain unverified.

claims.claim: Digital twins and shadows provide component monitoring evidence
claims.assessment: The authors qualify the evidence. Port and trunk-pipeline architectures provide transfer context rather than full CCUS control validation.

claims.claim: Training bias, distribution shift and safeguards limit learned policies
claims.assessment: A filter still needs a valid model, calibrated uncertainty and a verified operating domain. No safety result is reproduced.

claims.claim: Coupled planning should preserve a common objective and system feasibility
claims.assessment: The compact equations do not fully specify incidence or delivery. A disclosed analyst counterexample demonstrates the missing links.

claims.claim: Benders and ADMM are described as coordination architectures
claims.assessment: No native cuts, convergence proof or implementation is supplied. Standard convex guarantees do not automatically apply to discrete nonconvex cases.

claims.claim: The terminal definitions are said to link allocations to network flows
claims.assessment: The display defines allocation totals but shows no incidence relation to arc flow; it is an incomplete illustration.

claims.claim: Porthos illustrates shared trunks and staged access at a dated snapshot
claims.assessment: This is a 4 August 2026 snapshot. A nominal stock/rate ratio does not establish operating life, service availability or permission.

claims.claim: Northern Lights illustrates a ship–terminal–pipeline chain and phased capacity
claims.assessment: Nominal phased capacity is not a guarantee of present access, utilization or operational availability.

claims.claim: The Summit Iowa filing concerns a proposed 688-mile pipeline scope
claims.assessment: The claim concerns the Iowa proposed/permitting scope. Only its unit conversion is checked.

claims.claim: Li et al. report a national model with 1,186 sources and 329 sinks
claims.assessment: The reported candidate/shared layout is a model output, not built infrastructure or a transferable runtime boundary.

claims.claim: Transport-mode applicability depends on volume, distance and utilization
claims.assessment: The map explicitly has no numeric thresholds. Complete service and logistics conditions can alter the preferred mode.

claims.claim: Pipeline and shipping cost ranges have different case boundaries
claims.assessment: Currencies, years, volumes and boundaries differ. These ranges cannot establish a matched ranking or utility inventory.

claims.claim: The shortest route need not minimize total cost
claims.assessment: The conceptual distinction is reasonable; no native raster, routing cost surface or engineering case is reproduced.

claims.claim: Impurities, phase conditions and materials affect pipeline design
claims.assessment: Species, water content, temperature and phase domains need the originals. No universal impurity limit is adopted.

claims.claim: Governance can enter as costs, eligibility rules or scenarios
claims.assessment: Empirical acceptance and permitting can remain exogenous. These recommendations do not establish current legal access.

claims.claim: Budiarto is cited as an example of Pareto multiple-objective modelling
claims.assessment: The inspected original has one cost objective and scenario sensitivity, not a demonstrated Pareto frontier.

claims.claim: Becattini and Budiarto are cited for lifecycle emissions or abatement-cost objectives
claims.assessment: Budiarto's inspected cost/storage results do not provide a full LCA or LCOA. Becattini's exact support remains unverified in this check.

claims.claim: Hasan is described as extending SimCCS to include capture investment
claims.assessment: The 2009 original already includes capture investment. This does not judge the specific additional contributions of Hasan 2014.

claims.claim: The basic objective is described as discounted full-chain cost
claims.assessment: The expression has no displayed discount/horizon or variable capture-cost term. Scope, service target and cost basis remain incomplete.

claims.claim: The hub conservation expression requires an intermediate-node set
claims.assessment: The prose supplies the intermediate-node set, but the printed expression ends after the membership symbol. No correction is silently substituted.

claims.claim: Annual injection is bounded by a cumulative storage resource
claims.assessment: The stated units require a lifetime conversion or duration-weighted mass integral. A numeric rate-stock comparison cannot calibrate service.

claims.claim: Flow–diameter capacity bounds are associated with pressure and phase conditions
claims.assessment: Bounds alone do not impose pressure, temperature or phase stability. Valid preprocessing or additional equations are needed.

claims.claim: Each static arc can select at most one diameter
claims.assessment: The binary inequality correctly means at most one static option. It does not describe parallel pipes, replacement or upgrades.

claims.claim: The 2009 SimCCS paper is credited with a multiperiod dynamic framework
claims.assessment: The exact original explicitly states no temporal component and converts quantities to a 25-year lifetime basis, contradicting this attribution.

claims.claim: New-construction variables are said to prevent repeated capital charges
claims.assessment: A construction-event cost needs asset-stock, persistence and expansion links. The full dynamic case is not defined locally.

claims.claim: A robust min–max template is discussed alongside multistage recourse
claims.assessment: The displayed min-max is static and lacks a recourse policy and nonanticipativity. No adaptive value is reproduced.

claims.claim: Exact and decomposition methods can supply conditional solution bounds
claims.assessment: Guarantees depend on valid formulations, cuts, convergence and tolerances. No universal computational advantage follows.

claims.claim: Metaheuristics are described as offering near-optimal solutions with less computation
claims.assessment: Near-optimality and lower computational cost need repeated runs, meaningful bounds and matched budgets, rather than an algorithm label.

claims.claim: Table 6 lists SimCCS solver and runtime as not reported
claims.assessment: The original names ILOG CPLEX 11.0. Runtime and gap remain unestablished by the selected passages.

claims.claim: Hasan case scenarios concern 50–80% stationary-source reductions
claims.assessment: These are scenario reduction quantities, not accuracy or optimality metrics. The original cases remain unverified.

claims.claim: The Thailand AHA case has four candidate sinks
claims.assessment: This is an attributed case summary, not a reproduced optimum or a global certificate.

claims.claim: Bogs computation metadata and runtime cap are transcribed
claims.assessment: These are reported metadata. The maximum runtime below the cap is compatible; no native benchmark has been rerun.

claims.claim: Solver gaps and approximation or regret errors are different metrics
claims.assessment: Solver, approximation and regret errors are different quantities and must not be combined into a single accuracy measure.

claims.claim: More piecewise-linear segments change reported error and runtime
claims.assessment: The arithmetic is checkable, but different approximation and timing cases do not establish a universal causal ranking.

claims.claim: Joint uncertainty and information-dependent recourse remain limited
claims.assessment: This is a corpus-dependent frequency claim requiring the missing matrix and individual originals.

claims.claim: Solver bounds do not establish physical model validity
claims.assessment: This is an evaluation principle, not independent validation of the cited physical models.

claims.claim: Single-run or weak-baseline comparisons can exaggerate heuristic gains
claims.assessment: The recommendation is methodological; no quantitative bias estimate is supplied or reproduced.

claims.claim: AI training cost, distribution shift and feasibility require explicit tests
claims.assessment: These are evaluation conditions for proposed methods, not a demonstration of operational network control.

claims.claim: Hybrid candidate generation, exact repair and updated states are proposed
claims.assessment: This is a proposed architecture rather than a new implementation or controlled experiment.

claims.claim: Changing participation motivates entry, exit and ramp-up decisions
claims.assessment: Budiarto's fixed-source allocation does not demonstrate endogenous entry and exit. Other original support remains unverified.

claims.claim: Product-dependent utilization is distinct from durable storage
claims.assessment: Product demand and carbon fate are not assumed permanent. The cited market and lifecycle evidence remains unverified.

claims.claim: Infrastructure, data, liability and finance affect investability
claims.assessment: These are conditional institutional requirements. They do not provide quantified availability or a local service contract.

claims.claim: Digital twins are forecast to progress toward bounded decision support
claims.assessment: The forecast depends on interfaces, calibration and safeguards. It is not an achieved result.

claims.claim: Multi-agent learning is proposed for separate operators
claims.assessment: Agent-based transport and Markov games do not alone prove stable multi-operator learned control.

claims.claim: Markets and cooperative allocation may shape future networks
claims.assessment: This is a research direction, without demonstrated budget balance, cost recovery or coalition stability here.

claims.claim: Hydrogen synergies require operating-profile and alternative-use comparisons
claims.assessment: Synergies cannot be assumed; native coupled profiles, energy inventories and alternative-use comparisons are needed.

claims.claim: No realistic quantum advantage is reported within the 86-reference corpus
claims.assessment: This is an absence statement within the reported corpus, not an independent global search or hardware test.

claims.claim: RQ1 proposes a physically valid benchmark above 1,000 sources and 300 sinks
claims.assessment: The scale is a proposed evaluation target, not an achieved physically valid national model.

claims.claim: RQ2 proposes matched static and perfect-information comparisons
claims.assessment: The proposed metrics require matched information and scenarios; no calibrated recovery or value-of-information case is supplied.

claims.claim: RQ3 proposes governance and distributional evaluation criteria
claims.assessment: These are governance evaluation criteria, not established commercial arrangements.

claims.claim: RQ4 proposes total-computation and feasibility benchmarks for AI
claims.assessment: This is a benchmark proposal and not proof of AI advantage.

claims.claim: RQ5 proposes validation requirements for closed-loop digital twins
claims.assessment: These are validation requirements, not an operationally assured twin.

claims.assessment: The bibliography also contains books, reports and web sources. No complete machine-readable 17-study matrix is retained locally.

claims.assessment: The declarations document provenance; they neither establish an error nor validate the scientific content.

claims.assessment: All 86 entries are read and preserved. Two scoped checks do not verify the other 84 originals or close recursive source chains.
